12348-richard-vandermarck-a-novel.title: Richard Vandermarck A Novel
12348-richard-vandermarck-a-novel.creator: Mrs. Sidney S. Harris
12348-richard-vandermarck-a-novel.description: A book by Mrs. Sidney S. Harris. A very dull life indeed. I wonder how I endured it. The rooms were so dismal, the windows so uneventful. If it had not been for a room in the garret where I had my playthings, and where the sun came all day long, I am sure I should have been a much worse and more unhappy child.

arxiv-2209-06706.title: A Rigidity Result for the Robin Torsion Problem
arxiv-2209-06706.creator: Alba Lia Masiello, Gloria Paoli*
arxiv-2209-06706.description: Abstract Let Ω ⊂ ℝ 2 \Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{2} be an open, bounded and Lipschitz set. We consider the torsion problem for the Laplace operator associated to Ω \Omega with Robin boundary conditions. In this setting, we study the equality case in the Talenti-type comparison, proved in [ 5 ] .

arxiv-2211-14438.title: BERN-NN: Tight Bound Propagation For Neural Networks Using Bernstein Polynomial Interval Arithmetic
arxiv-2211-14438.creator: Wael Fatnassi, Haitham Khedr, Valen Yamamoto, Yasser Shoukry
arxiv-2211-14438.description: Abstract . In this paper, we present BERN-NN as an efficient tool to perform bound propagation of Neural Networks (NNs). Bound propagation is a critical step in wide range of NN model checkers and reachability analysis tools. Given a bounded input set, bound propagation algorithms aim to compute tight bounds on the output of the NN.

arxiv-2212-11139.title: High accuracy synchrotron radiation interferometry with relativistic electrons
arxiv-2212-11139.creator: P Klag 1, P Achenbach 1,2, T Akiyama 3, R Böhm 4, M O Distler 1, L Doria 1, P Eckert 1, A Esser 1, J Geratz 1, T Gogami 5, C Helmel 1, P Herrmann 1,6, M Hoek 1, M Kaneta 3, Y Konishi 3, R Kino 3, W Lauth 1, H Merkel 1, M Mizuno 3, U Müller 1, S Nagao 7, S N Nakamura 3,7, K Okuyama 3, J Pochodzalla 1
arxiv-2212-11139.description: Abstract A high-precision hypernuclear experiment has been performed at the Mainz Microtron (MAMI) to determine the hypertriton Λ \Lambda binding energy via decay-pion spectroscopy. A key element of this measurement is an accurate calibration of the magnetic spectrometers with the MAMI beam.

arxiv-2302-07710.title: A counterexample to strong local monomialization in a tower of two independent defect Artin-Schreier extensions Thanks: Partially supported by NSF grant DMS-2054394
arxiv-2302-07710.creator: Steven Dale Cutkosky
arxiv-2302-07710.description: Abstract . We give an example of an extension of two dimensional regular local rings in a tower of two independent defect Artin-Schreier extensions for which strong local monomialization does not hold. 2000 Mathematics Subject Classification primary 14B05; secondary 14B25, 13A18 1. Introduction In characteristic zero, there is a very nice local form for morphisms, called local monomialization.

arxiv-2308-16497.title: Moore-Penrose Dagger Categories
arxiv-2308-16497.creator: Robin Cockett, Jean-Simon Pacaud Lemay
arxiv-2308-16497.description: Abstract The notion of a Moore-Penrose inverse (M-P inverse) was introduced by Moore in 1920 and rediscovered by Penrose in 1955. The M-P inverse of a complex matrix is a special type of inverse which is unique, always exists, and can be computed using singular value decomposition.

arxiv-2405-16598.title: Regularized Projection Matrix Approximation with Applications to Community Detection Journal: Pattern Recognition
arxiv-2405-16598.creator: Zheng Zhai, Jialu Xu, Mingxin Wu, Xiaohui Li
arxiv-2405-16598.description: Abstract This paper introduces a regularized projection matrix approximation framework designed to recover cluster information from the affinity matrix. The model is formulated as a projection approximation problem, incorporating an entry-wise penalty function. We investigate three distinct penalty functions, each specifically tailored to address bounded, positive, and sparse scenarios.

arxiv-2406-03762.title: CORTEX: Large-Scale Brain Simulator Utilizing Indegree Sub-Graph Decomposition on Fugaku Supercomputer
arxiv-2406-03762.creator: Tianxiang Lyu, Mitsuhisa Sato, Shigeki Aoki, Ryutaro Himeno, Zhe Sun
arxiv-2406-03762.description: Abstract We introduce CORTEX, an algorithmic framework designed for large-scale brain simulation. Leveraging the computational capacity of the Fugaku Supercomputer, CORTEX maximizes available problem size and processing performance. Our primary innovation, Indegree Sub-Graph Decomposition, along with a suite of parallel algorithms, facilitates efficient domain decomposition by segmenting the global graph structure into smaller, identically structured sub-graphs.

arxiv-2411-04231.title: On the Work of Cartan and Münzner on Isoparametric Hypersurfaces
arxiv-2411-04231.creator: Thomas E. Cecil, Patrick J. Ryan
arxiv-2411-04231.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Thomas E. Cecil, Patrick J. Ryan. A hypersurface M n M^{n} in a real space form 𝐑 n + 1 {\bf R}^{n+1} , S n + 1 S^{n+1} , or H n + 1 H^{n+1} is isoparametric if it has constant principal curvatures. This paper is a survey of the fundamental work of Cartan and Münzner on the theory of isoparametric hypersurfaces in real space forms, in particular, spheres.

arxiv-2412-00979.title: Hierarchical Prompt Decision Transformer: Improving Few-Shot Policy Generalization with Global and Adaptive Guidance Conference: Companion Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2025 ; April 28 - May 02, 2025; Sydney, Australia
arxiv-2412-00979.creator: Zhe Wang, Haozhu Wang, Yanjun Qi
arxiv-2412-00979.description: Abstract . Decision transformers recast reinforcement learning as a conditional sequence generation problem, offering a simple but effective alternative to traditional value or policy-based methods. A recent key development in this area is the integration of prompting in decision transformers to facilitate few-shot policy generalization.

arxiv-2511-02012.creator: Zhexing Zhang

We estimate the L 2 ​ ( M ) → L q ​ ( Σ ) L^{2}(M)\to L^{q}(\Sigma) norm of a log \log -scale spectral projection operator.

pmc-12578334.title: Predicting residue ionization of OmpF channel using Constant pH Molecular Dynamics as benchmark
pmc-12578334.creator: Ernesto Tavares-Neto, Marcel Aguilella-Arzo, Vicente M. Aguilella
pmc-12578334.description: Electrostatic interactions are crucial for protein structure and function, especially in mesoscopic protein channels where ion selectivity is largely governed by the protein’s electrostatic properties. Understanding the protonation state of ionizable residues across pH values —often described by their pKa— is key to linking structure and function.

pmc-12612663.title: Bailout Left Atrial Appendage Closure implantation following Left atrial appendage perforation—a case report
pmc-12612663.creator: Hannes Alessandrini, Jan Per Wenzel, Charlotte Eitel, Darko Trajanoski, Roland Richard Tilz
pmc-12612663.description: risk of thromboembolism, endovascular LAA occlusion (LAAO) has become an important adjunctive therapy.2 We report the case of a 76-year-old woman scheduled for elective LAAO following successful electrical isolation. Her medical history included persistent AF (EHRA class III) and hypothyroidism treated with thyroxine. After ultrasound-guided transseptal puncture, a steerable coronary sinus catheter (WEBSTER® CS Catheter) was introduced to verify isolation.

pmc-12722586.title: Preliminary evaluation of image quality in supine breast MRI using a dedicated wearable coil and accelerometer-based motion correction
pmc-12722586.creator: Alexandre Megel, Karyna Isaieva, Lena Nohava, Freddy Odille, Marc Fauvel, Barbara Fischer, Elmar Laistler, Jacques Felblinger, Philippe Henrot
pmc-12722586.description: AbstractSupine breast MRI offers easier comparison with other screening methods than the prone MRI, but is often impaired by respiratory artifacts. This study aims to identify a suitable acceleration technique for motion-corrected supine breast MRI with a dedicated wearable coil (BraCoil), and to assess the quality of the resulting images. This prospective, single-center study included ten healthy female volunteers.

To inform decisions about harmonizing existing models, a deeper understanding of their delivery and impact on patient-relevant and health-economic outcomes is needed.

pmc-13601738.title: Understanding Multiple Intelligences Among Older Adults: Development and Validation of the Multiple Intelligence Scale for Older People
pmc-13601738.creator: Tzu‐Yu Lin, Ikeuchi Tomoko, I‐Hua Chen, Servet Üztemur, Mark D Griffiths, Chung‑Ying Lin
pmc-13601738.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPrevious studies have supported a multidimensional view of intelligence, particularly the concept of multiple intelligence (MI). However, the application and comprehensive understanding of MI in the context of aging have been explored infrequently. The present study aimed to develop and validate the Multiple Intelligence Scale for Older People (MISFOP) for community‐dwelling older adults, incorporating spiritual intelligence and ensuring cultural sensitivity through translation, adaptation, and psychometric validation.MethodsThe research comprised two studies to develop and validate the Chinese MISFOP.
